summary: Feeds Fun is a self-hosted news reader designed to help you aggregate web feeds. It includes organisation via tags, item scoring, and integrated artificial intelligence features for processing content. As a Python-based web application, it serves as an alternative to traditional RSS clients.
goodFor: This is a suitable choice if you want an RSS reader that experiments with AI-driven content sorting and categorisation. It fits hobbyists looking to test alternative news aggregation tools.
watchOut: The project lacks a tagged release history and shows signs of being at-risk regarding long-term maintenance. You may encounter bugs or incomplete features without stable milestone releases to rely upon.
deployNotes: As a Python application, it will typically require a WSGI or ASGI server, a persistent volume for data storage, and a reverse proxy such as Nginx to handle TLS termination. You should also check if it requires a separate relational database depending on its configuration.
